sections.h2: Where are the Bollinger County tax offices?
sections.html:
The county offices share one address, 204 High Street in Marble Hill, Missouri 63764, and one main number, 573-238-1900. The table below lists the offices that matter for a sale. Ask for the Collector when you call about a bill and for the Assessor about a value.

Bollinger County offices at 204 High Street, from the Missouri Association of Counties directory
OfficeLocation and phone
AssessorSuite 1, 573-238-1900 ext. 1
CollectorSuite 2, 573-238-1900
County ClerkSuite 5, 573-238-1900
RecorderSuite 7, 573-238-1900
TreasurerSuite 8, 573-238-1900

Marble Hill holds the courthouse and is the sole city. Glen Allen, Sedgewickville and Zalma are villages. The county was organized in March 1851 from parts of Wayne, Cape Girardeau and Stoddard counties and is named for George Frederick Bollinger, who brought German settlers to the area in 1799 and 1800. Marble Hill was first called Dallas and took its present name in 1865.

sections.h2: What does selling in Bollinger County involve?
sections.html:
Bollinger County is rural throughout. The 2020 census counted 10,567 people over 618 square miles of land, about 17 per square mile, and classified none of them as urban. Terrain climbs from flat delta country in the south to Ozark hills in the north, Routes 34, 51 and 72 carry traffic, and part of the Mark Twain National Forest lies inside the county. Blue Pond, the deepest natural pond in Missouri, is in the south.

The county is split among four school districts: Woodland R-IV at Marble Hill, Leopold R-III, Meadow Heights R-II at Patton and Zalma R-V. Three Rivers College covers the area. Commutes are long, with a mean travel time to work of 35.5 minutes compared with about 18 minutes in Boone or Buchanan County. On April 5, 2023, an EF2 tornado struck Glen Allen and Grassy and killed five people.

sections.h2: How do Bollinger County housing figures read?
sections.html:
QuickFacts lists these figures for Bollinger County.

  • Housing units in 2025: 5,045
  • Share of households that own, 2020-2024: 82.3 percent
  • Typical owner-occupied home value: $179,800
  • Median gross rent: $694
  • Median household income: $63,814
  • Residents 65 and over: 22.8 percent
  • Building permits in 2025: 0

Applying the 19 percent residential rate listed by the Boone County Collector, a $179,800 house has an assessed value near $34,162. The 2020 census also found 17.1 percent of the 5,037 housing units vacant, a higher share than the 8.0 percent in Boone County or 11.4 percent in Buchanan County.

sections.h2: When are Bollinger County property taxes due?
sections.html:
Missouri sets the deadline at December 31 for every county, and Bollinger is no exception. State guidance says unpaid balances pick up interest and penalties after that day, and RSMo 139.100 treats a mailed payment as timely if the postmark falls inside the period. For bill timing, accepted payment types and the current mailing address, call 573-238-1900 and ask for the Collector.

For land that goes unpaid, RSMo 140.100 adds an 18 percent penalty on the year's delinquency, or at most 2 percent per month when redeemed before a sale. The tax sale falls on the fourth Monday in August, which was August 24 in 2026, and that date has passed.

sections.h2: How does the Bollinger County tax sale work?
sections.html:
RSMo 140.150 makes land with unpaid taxes or special assessments subject to sale on the fourth Monday in August each year. A few protections come with that.

  • The collector must mail a first class notice to the recorded owner before delinquent land is published for sale.
  • A second notice by certified mail is required when the assessed value is above $1,000.
  • If the certified notice comes back unsigned, a further first class notice goes to the owner and to any occupant.
  • Tax, penalty, interest and costs can be paid to the county collector at any time before the sale.

The statute also says that not receiving a notice does not cancel the tax. A seller who has moved should update the mailing address with the Collector's office, because notices go to the recorded owner.

sections.h2: Who is likely to buy a house in Bollinger County?
sections.html:
The buyer pool is small and local. The county is part of the Cape Girardeau metropolitan area, and Wikipedia describes its economy as resting mainly on agriculture and construction. QuickFacts records 200 employer establishments and 1,396 jobs in 2023, down 2.9 percent from 2022, and retail sales of $8,970 per resident in 2022, so most shopping and many jobs sit outside the county line.

The 2020 census put the median age at 45.5 and found 4,177 households, 80.1 percent of them owner-occupied. Only 13.9 percent of adults hold a bachelor's degree, and 81.3 percent of households have a broadband subscription. Those facts point to long-term owners, family transfers and buyers who commute toward Cape Girardeau or Perryville. A realistic asking price, a clear tax record and a prompt closing usually count for more than staging.

sections.h2: How can a Bollinger County owner challenge an assessment?
sections.html:
Begin with the Assessor's office at 204 High Street, Suite 1. The Assessor values real and personal property each year, and the office can explain the factors used. Next comes the county Board of Equalization, where the filing deadline is the second Monday in July.

The state level is the Missouri State Tax Commission. Under RSMo 138.430 an owner may appeal the board's ruling within the time set by statute or 30 days after final action, whichever is later, and the Commission's guidance says the form can be filed online, by email or by mail to PO Box 146, Jefferson City, MO 65102. An appeal for property owned by a corporation, LLC, trust or estate must come from an attorney.

An owner who wants to dispute value without missing the payment deadline can pay under protest. The State Tax Commission describes the steps as paying the whole bill by December 31, marking the check, and filing a written statement with the Collector that states the claimed market value.

sections.h2: What should a Bollinger County seller check before closing?
sections.html:
Treat the tax bill as part of the sale price discussion. Real estate tax follows the land, so a buyer takes the property subject to anything unpaid. A title company will normally order a tax search, and a seller can skip surprises by calling the Collector for the balance and asking whether any prior year is open.

If the Assessor holds the wrong mailing address, or the legal description on file differs from the deed, correct it before listing. The Recorder in Suite 7 keeps the deed record, and the Treasurer in Suite 8 is a separate office from the Collector. Ask each one for its own instructions rather than assuming the same counter handles them all.

faqs.q: What is the Bollinger County property tax deadline?
faqs.a: December 31, the statewide deadline. Call 573-238-1900 and ask for the Collector to confirm how and where to pay.

faqs.q: Where is the Bollinger County Assessor?
faqs.a: At 204 High Street, Suite 1, Marble Hill, MO 63764. The main number is 573-238-1900, extension 1 for the Assessor.

faqs.q: When is the Bollinger County tax sale?
faqs.a: The fourth Monday in August under state law. That was August 24 in 2026, so the next one falls on the fourth Monday of August 2027.

faqs.q: Can unpaid taxes be paid before the sale?
faqs.a: Yes. RSMo 140.150 lets an owner pay the delinquent tax, penalty, interest and costs to the collector at any time before the property is sold.
The Census Bureau estimates 10,646 for 2025, up 0.7 percent from the 2020 count of 10,567, spread across 618 square miles of land.
